text:
jia: Pushed A100 vs H100 sweep for LlamaX-13B q4f16 across us-west1 / eu-central1. Quick thread with highlights and a weird tail in eu-central H100.

jia: Results snapshot (on-demand pricing, seq distribution mixed: 128/512/1024/2048)
```
Model: LlamaX-13B q4f16
Region       | GPU   | prefill p50/p95 (ms) | decode p50/p95 (ms) | tokens/sec | $/1M tokens
us-west1     | A100  | 120 / 240            | 8 / 60              | 95         | $18
us-west1     | H100  | 95  / 200            | 7 / 45              | 135        | $15
eu-central1  | A100  | 140 / 300            | 9 / 70              | 88         | $20
eu-central1  | H100  | 125 / 520            | 10 / 480            | 60         | $22  <-- high decode tail on long seq
```

jia: Notes: prefill = full seq attention build, decode = streaming token gen. eu-central H100 p95 decode spikes on seq>=1024. Kernel traces show a fallback on a couple of kernels during long-seq runs.

alex: can you paste the kernel trace snippet? batch size / seq / concurrency used?

jia: run cmd + trace:
```
./bench --model llamaX-13b --quant q4f16 --gpu h100 --region eu-central1 --seq 2048 --batch 1 --qps 10 --trace kernels
... KERNEL TRACE ...
KERNEL_FALLBACK: aten_addmm_fp32 -> non-quantized path -> net_latency spike
PCIe_STALLS: minor, but NVLINK ok
```

matt: if it's falling back to fp32 conv path that's consistent with huge decode tail. Could be missing optimized cuBLAS kernel for this quant layout. Any kernel id in the trace?

jia: kernel id 0x7a3f flagged. Also saw increased memcpy times when seq>1024.

matt: try forcing the quant-friendly kernel set or reduce max_seq to 1024 as a mitigation. Also check driver (we're on 535.54) and libtorch/aten builds.

sophie: FYI the $/1M numbers assume on-demand hour rates; reserved pricing will change the economics. For routing decisions we should compute both spot/on-demand and reserved.

jia: ack — current numbers = on-demand. I'll re-run eu-central H100 with seq cap 1024 and a reserved-price cost model (committed) and post delta.

bench-bot: Scheduled job: 82432 — eu-central1 H100 seq<=1024, qps sweep 10/50/100, batch 1. ETA ~45m.

alex: If confirmed that H100 tail is kernel fallback, short-term routing policy: route seq<=1024 -> H100, seq>1024 -> A100 in eu-central. That preserves $/1M and avoids regen latency. Can someone draft a fallback policy?

sophie: I'll draft a policy with cost threshold and p95 latency SLO cutover. Also add an alert if decode p95 > 300ms for H100 in any region.

jia: One more datapoint: us-west H100 stable and cheaper per token for mixed seq workload; looks like the issue is region-specific (eu infra / driver / kernel builds).

alex: ok good. Next steps: (1) jia re-run reserved pricing/seq<=1024/throughput slice (2) matt triage kernel id and driver mismatch (3) sophie draft routing policy + alert.

jia: will post results in-thread when job finishes. Thanks. :thumbsup:
